content_of_post_to_comment:
People harp on about social media as a whole but has there been any research done on the general every day use of posting behind a screen where nobody can see your identity. *forgive me, as this seems a bit hypocritical haha

I appreciate amongst a lot of good replies and comments we always tend to fixate on the negative, but when we post every day on reddit for example, and someone always picks apart our opinions is this not damaging to our mental health?

I hope this makes some sort of sense ...
comment: I've wondered about this too, because anonymity changes the dynamic in a weird way. A stranger picking apart an opinion can feel personal even when they don't know anything about you. At the same time, Reddit can also be a place where people get useful pushback they'd avoid in real life. Maybe the difference is whether we're using replies to refine our thoughts or using them as a measure of our own worth.
